10-24.text: 1973: CSUN dedicated its new library building, later known as the Oviatt Library and now the University Library.

10-25.text: 1960: Vice presidential nominee Lyndon B. Johnson held a campus rally at San Fernando Valley State College, now CSUN.

10-26.text: 1992: Metrolink commuter rail began service, including the Ventura County and Santa Clarita lines through the Valley.

10-27.text: 1920: Olive View Sanatorium, a county tuberculosis hospital, opened in what is now Sylmar.

10-29.text: 2005: Metro's Orange Line busway opened, linking North Hollywood and Warner Center across the Valley.

10-30.text: 1980: The Sherman Oaks Galleria opened on Ventura Boulevard with Robinson's and May Company as anchors.

11-01.text: 1938: The community of North Los Angeles, once called Zelzah, changed its name to Northridge.

11-02.text: 1950: A replica adobe at Campo de Cahuenga, where the 1847 Treaty of Cahuenga was signed, was dedicated.

11-04.text: 1968: Black students occupied Valley State College's administration building, a protest that led to ethnic studies at CSUN.

11-05.text: 1913: The Los Angeles Aqueduct opened at the Cascades in Sylmar before a crowd of more than 30,000.
2002: Los Angeles voters rejected Measure F, the proposal for the San Fernando Valley to secede and form its own city.

11-06.text: 1990: A fire on the Universal Studios backlot destroyed New York Street and badly damaged Courthouse Square.

11-08.text: 1965: NBC's 'Days of Our Lives,' taped at the network's Burbank studios, premiered on television.
2016: Burbank voters approved Measure B, clearing the way for a new 14-gate terminal at Hollywood Burbank Airport.

11-10.text: 1958: Bob Hope hit the first drive to open L.A. County's new Knollwood Golf Course on Balboa Boulevard in Granada Hills.

11-14.text: 1960: The city dedicated the new West Valley branch library on Vanowen Street in Reseda.

11-15.text: 1955: A coordinated traffic signal system switched on along 11 miles of Ventura Boulevard, from North Hollywood to Tarzana.
2004: The new Chatsworth Branch Library on Devonshire Street held its grand opening.

11-16.text: 1961: A new Senior Citizens Center officially opened at North Hollywood Playground on Tujunga Avenue.
2007: ArcLight Cinemas opened its Sherman Oaks theater at the Sherman Oaks Galleria.

11-17.text: 1963: Burbank formally dedicated its new $1.1 million Central Library on Glenoaks Boulevard.
2018: The Valley Relics Museum opened to the public in its new home at 7900 Balboa Blvd. at Van Nuys Airport.

11-18.text: 1961: Valley Presbyterian Hospital in Van Nuys dedicated its second phase, adding 120 beds.
1964: The Valley woke to snow on Oat Mountain and the hills above Chatsworth and Granada Hills after a cold storm.

11-19.text: 1962: L.A. Fire Station No. 97 on Mulholland Drive above Studio City was dedicated with an open house.

11-22.text: 1924: Franklin Canyon Road opened through the Santa Monica foothills, per the Daily News' Valley history timeline.
2019: "Frozen II," made by Walt Disney Animation Studios in Burbank, opened in U.S. theaters.

11-24.text: 1911: The Van Nuys Call, forerunner of today's Daily News, was first published under the name The Van Nuys News.

11-26.text: 2021: Paul Thomas Anderson's "Licorice Pizza," set in the 1973 San Fernando Valley, opened in limited release.

11-28.text: 1797: The first baptism was recorded in the new church at Mission San Fernando Rey de Espana, founded that September.

12-01.text: 1937: Pollard-Carrell Chevrolet, one of the Valley's first Chevrolet dealerships, opened on San Fernando Road in San Fernando.
1977: Have Blue, the stealth demonstrator from Lockheed's Burbank Skunk Works, made its first flight in Nevada.
1989: "National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation," with the Griswold house set at the Warner Bros. Ranch in Burbank, was released.

12-03.text: 1945: A Burbank-built Lockheed Constellation left Washington on TWA's first transatlantic proving flight to Paris.
1968: Elvis Presley's comeback TV special, taped that June at NBC Studios in Burbank, aired on NBC.

12-04.text: 2023: Los Angeles Mission College in Sylmar opened its new Student Services and Administration Building.

12-06.text: 1806: The new adobe church at Mission San Fernando Rey de España was blessed by Fray Pedro Muñoz.
1957: Lockheed's L-188 Electra, the first American turboprop airliner, made its first flight from Burbank.
2011: Universal Studios Hollywood announced plans for The Wizarding World of Harry Potter.

12-07.text: 1912: Pacific Electric extended its Valley rail line west from Van Nuys to Owensmouth, today's Canoga Park.

12-10.text: 1938: The first Lockheed Hudson, a bomber built for Britain's Royal Air Force, began flight trials in Burbank.
1958: Ritchie Valens played a homecoming concert at Pacoima Junior High, later released as a live album.

12-16.text: 1911: Pacific Electric red cars began running over Cahuenga Pass to Van Nuys, opening rail service to the Valley.

12-17.text: 1928: Metropolitan Airport, today's Van Nuys Airport, opened on the 25th anniversary of the Wright brothers' flight.
2003: Burbank's airport was renamed Bob Hope Airport for the longtime Toluca Lake resident.

12-19.text: 1997: Los Angeles named Harvester Farms on Devonshire Street in Chatsworth a Historic-Cultural Monument.

12-21.text: 1962: The San Diego Freeway's 5.7-mile section through the Sepulveda Pass, linking the Valley and the Westside, was dedicated.
1968: Apollo 8 launched for the Moon on F-1 engines built by Rocketdyne in Canoga Park.

12-22.text: 1964: The SR-71 Blackbird, developed by Lockheed's Burbank-based Skunk Works, made its first flight.

12-27.text: 1924: Mulholland Highway opened amid much fanfare along the ridge between the Valley and the L.A. basin.
1958: Pacoima's Ritchie Valens performed "Donna" on The Dick Clark Show.

12-31.text: 2012: Universal Studios Hollywood closed T2-3D: Battle Across Time to make way for Despicable Me Minion Mayhem.
